taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: MCP OAuth registration profiles and client-metadata-to-consent binding
controls.source_trace: Trace a client identity/redirect through registration to granted resource authority, including reuse of client metadata across protected MCP resources.
controls.implementation_branch: Distinguish registration metadata from user consent and from authorization-server identity. Dynamic registration can be a supported public-client flow. Pin the redirect/client relationship and broker transaction so an attacker client cannot reuse another client consent; a new valid client record by itself is not a successful impersonation or token disclosure.
controls.operational_method: Identify the actual registration profile first: pre-registered clients, dynamic registration or supported client-metadata documents are different trust paths. Retain client metadata provenance, redirect selection and the exact client identity displayed/recorded at consent. Compare a legitimate client update with an untrusted metadata/redirect change; open registration alone is expected under some profiles. Generic wrong-resource token validation remains the MCP authorization workflow.
controls.controlled_verification: In the chosen registration profile, retain registered metadata and consent transaction for two owned clients. Compare legitimate creation/update with a changed redirect or metadata provenance and inspect the client identity receiving the resulting grant.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Dynamic registration can be intentional; a client ID alone grants no user/resource permission.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Bind registration and consent to the intended client/resource and preserve legitimate compatible clients.
